charter:
# Charter — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** S06c 'MCP Tasks', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 7
- **Delivered:** the MCP task protocol over the conveyor's own `/mcp` surface. `projects.execute` returns `resultType:"task"`; `tasks/get` lists the project's pending approvals as `inputRequests`; `tasks/update` answers one through `approvals.decide`; a terminal run is a terminal result with `isError` for failure. The task id is the run id, no new table is added and no Python service sits in the path.
- **Authority:** the tranche-7 authorisation recorded by the tranche-6 review, exercised under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.
- **Acceptance:** `acceptance/programme/S06c.toml`, whose gate is the task round trip through a project that waits on an approval.
- **Closure:** the project is already closed in the record; this pack supplies the charter, baseline, artefact set, registers, contract, WBS deliverable, Phase-G review, outputs and closure review the row was closed without, then re-closes it through its own gate.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective, Phase A)

body.assignment: Deliver the architectural record for durable agent tasks: a client that declares the MCP task extension drives a long-running project — starting it, polling it, answering the approval it waits on and reading a terminal result — without a second store and without a service between the client and the conveyor. The assignment is retrospective: the product shipped on 2026-11-09 and this statement records the architecture it was built to.
body.scope: In scope: the Phase A–D artefact set, the task-to-run identity, the project-scoped `inputRequests` listing, the answer path through `approvals.decide`, and the two indexes migration 0023 adds. Out of scope: the agent's own task support against external MCP servers, decommissioning `mcp_server`, SSE or push delivery, a progress percentage, and any new table.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors the set under the standing delegation; the Architecture Board reviews it; the SRO is accountable for the agent interface; the MCP client author is the consumer whose conformance the contract is written against. The retrospective author is not the accepting role, so the separation of duties holds even though one session wrote the product record and this set.
body.acceptance_criteria: The manifest's checks, each with its own target: exactly one task-capable action read from the compiled registry; the project-scoped `inputRequests`; the answer written as `approvals.decide`; a terminal result that never says `failed` on the wire; one `-32602` for every ownership failure; and the parity suite proving the task surface and the HTTP action agree.
body.constraints: No new table and no new service. The run state machine is the task lifecycle, so the reaper had to learn to skip project executions and the one-live-run property had to become a partial unique index because the existing index does not dedupe nulls. Every constraint in this project is a consequence of the reuse decision rather than an independent choice.
body.retrospective: This statement is written after the fact and declares so. The slice plan's build record gives the shipped state; the gate's compiled-registry assertion is the one the plan had to correct, because its first form grepped a flag no serialised surface carries. That correction is recorded here rather than tidied away.

# Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — S06c MCP Tasks (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase A; plateau psa; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S06c; tranche 7; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. This artefact is authored by the retrospective rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

Three drivers. A long-running project must survive a client that disconnects — a call that blocks for a day is not a task, it is a stuck socket. A project waiting on a human must be answerable without a second channel — the approval already exists and polling it is enough. And the estate must not grow a second store — the run table already holds the lifecycle, so a task table would duplicate a fact.

## Links

Derives from `docs/plans/slices/S06c-mcp-tasks.md` §1 and §9; feeds the Requirements Catalog, which turns each driver into a checkable requirement; depends on the Stakeholder Map for ownership. The third driver is the one that constrains the other two: it rules out the obvious design, which is a tasks table with its own state machine.

## Document

The catalogue records why the task protocol was adopted rather than a bespoke polling endpoint, and why the reuse constraint is architectural rather than stylistic. A reader who treats the missing table as an omission will propose adding one; the catalogue is the place that explains why that proposal would duplicate the run lifecycle.

# Requirements Catalog — S06c MCP Tasks (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase A; plateau psa; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S06c; tranche 7; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. This artefact is authored by the retrospective rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

Five requirements. R1 exactly one task-capable action, `projects.execute`, read from the compiled registry. R2 `tasks/get` returns the pending approvals as `inputRequests` for the project, not for the run. R3 `tasks/update` answers an approval through `approvals.decide`. R4 a terminal run returns a terminal result with `isError` for failure, never a `failed` state on the wire. R5 every ownership failure returns the same `-32602`, so the endpoint is not an oracle.

## Links

Derives from the Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog; realized by the Solution Concept Diagram; sourced from `docs/plans/slices/S06c-mcp-tasks.md` §7, which names the exact test target behind each requirement. R1's check reads the compiled registry rather than a flag on a serialised action list, because that list carries no flags — a filter for one would match nothing and exit 0.

## Document

Each requirement carries one owning check in `acceptance/programme/S06c.toml`. R2's project-scoped listing is the subtle one: filtering `inputRequests` by run id hides every card-level gate, which is most of them, and the surface would look correct while answering nothing.

# Solution Concept Diagram — S06c MCP Tasks (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type diagram; phase A; plateau psa; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S06c; tranche 7; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. This artefact is authored by the retrospective rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

The concept is an identity, not a component: the task id is the run id. `projects.execute` opens a run and returns its id as a task. `tasks/get` reads that run and translates its pending approvals into `inputRequests`. `tasks/update` writes an `approvals.decide` against the same run. A terminal run is a terminal task, and `failed` is carried on the wire as a completed result with `isError`.

## Links

Realizes the Requirements Catalog; depends on the Business Capability Map and the Data Entity catalog; reuses the run state machine, the approval state machine and the `/mcp` transport the platform already ships. The diagram is prose because the artefact store holds text bodies; an image would be a second, unchecked source.

## Document

The concept deliberately adds no component. A reader looking for a task service will not find one, and that absence is the design: the identity between task and run is what makes the state machine, the reaper and the approval path work unchanged. The two partial indexes migration 0023 adds are the only new schema.

Type diagram; phase B; plateau hld; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S06c; tranche 7; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. ## Entries

Two capabilities. Durable execution lets a client start a project and stop listening without losing the work. Deferred answer lets a project block on a human and be resolved through the same protocol that started it. Both are exposed through `/mcp` and both reuse the run and approval state machines; neither adds a surface.

## Links

Derives from the Solution Concept Diagram and the Requirements Catalog; feeds the Data Entity and Technology Standards catalogs. The capability view is the client author's: what can a task-capable client do that a plain tool caller cannot, and the answer is start-and-leave plus answer-later.

## Document

The map is deliberately two capabilities rather than four. A progress percentage, a push channel and a cancellation verb all look like capabilities and are out of scope by the slice plan; recording them as capabilities would invite a later session to build them under this project's name.

# Data Entity/Data Component Catalog — S06c MCP Tasks (Phase C)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase C; plateau hld; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S06c; tranche 7; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. This artefact is authored by the retrospective rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

No new data entity. The task is the `run` row and its lifecycle is that row's state machine; the answer is the `approval` and its `approval_decision`. The only schema change is index-only: migration 0023 adds `uq_run_project_live`, a partial unique index because the existing `uq_run_live` does not dedupe nulls, and `approval_project_idx` for the project-scoped listing.

## Links

Derives from the Business Capability Map; realizes both capabilities over existing entities; depends on the Technology Standards catalog for the index and RLS conventions. Naming the absent entity is the point of this artefact: a data catalogue for a project that adds no table has to say so explicitly or a reader will assume the table was forgotten.

## Document

The partial index is a correctness fix as much as a performance one: a unique index that permits duplicates where a column is null lets two live executions of the same project coexist, so the task's one-live-run property would be a check in code rather than a constraint. Putting it in the schema removes the race rather than narrowing it.

# Technology Standards Catalog — S06c MCP Tasks (Phase D)

## Metadata

Type catalog; phase D; plateau hld; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S06c; tranche 7; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. This artefact is authored by the retrospective rework and does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

Three standards. The MCP task protocol as the wire contract, so a conforming client needs no bespoke knowledge. The compiled action registry as the single source of task-capable actions, because the serialised action list carries no flags. And the ownership rule that every failure is one error code, because a distinguishable refusal is an oracle.

## Links

Derives from the Data Entity catalog; realizes the technology half of the Solution Concept Diagram; reuses the `/mcp` transport and the rmcp crate the platform already ships rather than adding a client library. Each standard names the failure it prevents, so the catalogue is enforceable in review.

## Document

No new technology is introduced. The registry entry has already cost a session time: the old check grepped for `task_capable: true`, a flag that exists in neither the admin dump nor the committed action list, so it could never match and its zero-match run exited green. The standard records the compiled registry as the source so the mistake is not repeated.

documents.title: User stories — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# User stories — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective, Phase G)

## Personas

An MCP client author who declares the `io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks` extension and expects a long-running project to behave as a protocol task rather than as a bespoke polling endpoint; and a conveyor operator who reads the run record to explain what a client observed. Both consume the same rows the run state machine already writes.

## Stories

- As an MCP client author, I want `projects.execute` to return `resultType: "task"` with the run id as the task id, so that I can poll `tasks/get` without a second endpoint or a second store.
- As a client that must answer an input request, I want `tasks/update` to carry my answer into `approvals.decide`, so that the run continues through the gate it was already waiting on.
- As an operator, I want a terminal run to expose one canonical result with `isError` on failure, so that the wire never reports `failed` because of a check-order artefact.

## Scenarios

S1 start → poll → answer → terminal result over `/mcp`; S2 an ownership failure returns one code regardless of which check caught it; S3 the surface is exactly one task-capable action and adds no table. The gate is the round trip, not a unit of the transport.

## Verify

`python3 scripts/rework-content-check.py --project S06c --content docs/evidence/rework/tranche-7/rework-content-S06c.json --snapshot /tmp/snap-7/data --wsjf 8,6,6,8 --closes true`, then the factory run and the receipt assertion in `docs/evidence/rework/S06c.json`; the product check reads the compiled registry for the single task-capable action `projects.execute`.

documents.body:
# Definition of ready — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective)

## Independent

The pack stands on its own row set: it reads the pinned snapshot `/tmp/snap-7` and writes only S06c's charter, baseline, artefacts, registers, contract, WBS deliverable and closure records. The other two tranche members share the snapshot and the four cadence rows, but no act of S06c depends on their products or moves their rows.

## Negotiable

The record set is the pack's scope; the review's decision (#755) and the production promotion (#852) are owned elsewhere. Within the set, the wording of the charter, the seven A–D artefacts and the closure review is the author's to negotiate with the standard, not a fixed template.

## Valuable

S06c is benefit `B1` (auditable decisions): the task surface makes the run the durable record of what a client asked, was asked, and got. A green receipt turns that claim into a checked record instead of a prose claim, which is what the tranche review needs.

## Estimable

The refinement record measures eight open record packages for S06c (0 P0, 8 P1): charter, baseline, contract, review, the seven artefacts, the closure set. The factory journals every act, so an interrupted run resumes at the member it stopped on.

## Small

One pack, one factory run, one receipt, one closure; no product rebuild and no cluster change. The whole unit is one branch and one pull request, and the pack is 45 KB of authored prose rather than generated volume.

## Testable

Every claim has an executable check: the offline content checker at the pinned snapshot, the factory's post-write receipt with one row per manifest check, and the tranche exit gate that refuses a stale or red receipt.

## Dependencies

S06c depends on S04 (the action registry and `/mcp` transport), S05 (project and card actions), S06 (run and approval state machines) and S06b (the licence principal and tool list). No dependency is outside a closed tranche.

# Definition of done — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective)

## Acceptance criteria

The manifest's seventeen checks are the acceptance criteria, and each is a row in `docs/evidence/rework/S06c.json`: the closed row, the approved baseline, the charter asset, the closure output, the live contract, the Phase-G review, the closure gate, the waivers, the PI set, the WSJF, the demo credit, the lesson, the product findings, the artefact standard and the rework resolution.

## Evidence at completion

The receipt `docs/evidence/rework/S06c.json` (verdict, per-check rows, `snapshot.git_sha = 7e93a325f`), the acts record and transcript under `docs/evidence/rework/S06c/`, the batch journal `docs/evidence/rework/batch/tranche-7.jsonl`, and the tranche exit `docs/evidence/rework/tranche-7/tranche-exit.json`.

## Repo gate

The unit's docs-only changes pass `git diff --check` and the design gates (`build-docs.py --check`, `check-docs.cjs`, `check-data.cjs`); the repository's GitHub preflight and `ci-public` are the compile/lint and final gates at the exact PR head.

## Merge and closure

One pull request closes #951 and merges after the exit is green; the project row closes through its own closure gate with a distinct approver, and the closure review is published as the declared closure output. The next tranche's authorisation is #755's act, not this unit's.

risk.title: The live one-live-run property depends on a partial index, because the existing unique index does not dedupe nulls
risk.body: `uq_run_live` permits two live rows when the discriminating column is null, so a check-then-insert in application code would let two live executions of the same project coexist under load. Migration 0023 adds a partial unique index. The risk that remains is a later migration dropping or widening it without knowing why it is partial.
risk.response: Keep the index's comment and this risk row as the record of why it is partial, and refuse a migration that replaces it with a full unique index on the same columns.

risk.title: The reaper must skip project executions, and its correctness depends on that predicate
risk.body: `reap_dead_runs_tx` now requires `card_id IS NOT NULL`, which is what keeps the reaper from killing a task that is legitimately waiting on a human for a day. If a later change relaxes the predicate, long-running tasks are reaped and the surface reports a cancellation nobody asked for.
risk.response: Cover the reaper's project-execution exclusion with a test that fails if the predicate is widened, and treat the predicate as part of this project's contract rather than as an implementation detail.

risk.title: The `failed` state must never reach the wire, which makes the terminal check ordering load-bearing
risk.body: A terminal run is surfaced as a completed result carrying `isError`, and the terminal check runs before the approval check. Reverse the order and a failed run with a stale pending approval reports `inputRequests` for a task that will never accept an answer; drop the terminal check entirely and the client polls a dead task forever.
risk.response: Assert both orderings in the contract suite: a failed run with a stale approval must terminate, not block.

issue.title: The record claimed built while carrying no charter, baseline, contract or Phase-G review
issue.body: At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the project row is closed and its product is in the tree, but the snapshot carries no charter asset, no approved baseline, no delivery contract, no Phase A–D set and no compliance review. The gap is a record gap rather than a product gap; this pack supplies the set and the receipt proves it.
issue.response: Supplied by this pack and proved by the project's receipt at the pinned snapshot.

issue.title: The gate's first form could never match, and its zero-match run exited green
issue.body: The plan's compiled-registry assertion originally grepped for `task_capable: true`, a flag carried by neither the admin action dump nor the committed action list. A filter that selects nothing exits 0, so a check that proved nothing read as a pass until the plan corrected it to read the compiled registry directly.
issue.response: The corrected assertion is the one the receipt runs; the mistake is recorded so the pattern is not reintroduced by a later zero-match filter.

issue.title: A progress percentage and push delivery are absent by scope, not by omission
issue.body: The task surface reports state transitions but no percentage and no server push; the client polls. Both absences are deliberate per the slice plan's boundary, but an MCP client author reading the protocol spec may expect them, so the absence needs a record rather than a silence.
issue.response: Document the polling-only contract in the project brief and treat a push or percentage request as a new unit rather than a defect in this one.

assumption.title: The 2026-11-28 rework snapshot is the authoritative record for S06c
assumption.body: Every judgement in this pack is read from the pinned snapshot, and the content checker refuses any identifier that appears nowhere in it. A row that changed after the snapshot is out of scope for this pack by construction.

assumption.title: A conforming MCP client accepts polling as the only delivery mechanism
assumption.body: The protocol allows push; this implementation does not provide it. The assumption is that a conforming client treats push as optional, which the slice plan's decisions assert when they keep polling as the fallback.

assumption.title: One live execution per project is the right cardinality
assumption.body: The partial unique index enforces it. The assumption is that a project is a single unit of concurrent work; if a project ever needs two live executions the index is the thing that will say so, loudly, at the second start.

assumption.title: The approval is a sufficient input request
assumption.body: The task's `inputRequests` are the project's pending approvals, and there is no other kind of input the surface accepts. A future input type — a form, a selection — would need its own mapping rather than a widening of the approval path.

dependency.title: S06c depends on S04, S05 and S06
dependency.body: The project row records the edges. S04 supplies the action registry and the `/mcp` transport, S05 the project and card actions, and S06 the run and approval state machines together with the events the task surface reads.

dependency.title: S06b supplies the licence principal the task surface authenticates
dependency.body: A task-capable call is still a licence-principal call; S06b's machine-auth resolution and tool list are what make the call attributable. Without that principal the task would be anonymous and the ownership failures would have nothing to compare.

dependency.title: S13 populates `statusMessage` and the agent's own task support is a separate plan
dependency.body: The task status text is S13's to fill and the agent's client-side task support against external servers is a separate plan with its own gate. Recording both stops a reader treating an empty status message as an S06c defect.

benefit.title: A long-running project becomes a durable task with no second store
benefit.body: Before the task protocol a client that disconnected lost the ability to follow the project without re-deriving its state from the run table. After it, the run is the task and the client polls a standard surface. The benefit is structural and is proved by the contract suite rather than by a measurement.

benefit.title: A blocked project is answerable through the protocol that started it
benefit.body: The `inputRequests` listing and the `tasks/update` answer mean a client needs one surface, not two, to start work and to unblock it. The benefit is observed in the single round-trip test that starts a project, receives a task, answers the approval and reads a terminal result.

benefit.title: One task-capable action keeps the surface small
benefit.body: `projects.execute` is the only action that returns a task, asserted against the compiled registry. A surface where every action could be a task would make the client's lifecycle handling universal and the server's contract unprovable; one action keeps both bounded.

benefit.title: Ownership failures are indistinguishable
benefit.body: Every ownership failure returns the same `-32602`, so the endpoint cannot be used to probe which project ids exist. The benefit is a security property and is measured by the suite that asserts one code across the failure cases.

project_brief_output:
# Project Brief — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome

An MCP client that declares the task extension drives a long-running project as a durable task: it calls `projects.execute`, receives a task, polls `tasks/get` through a project waiting on an approval, answers with `tasks/update` and reads a terminal result — with no Python service in the path and no new table.

## Boundary

S06c owns the task mapping over `/mcp`. It does not own the agent's client-side task support against external MCP servers, the decommissioning of `mcp_server`, SSE or push delivery, a progress percentage, or any new table.

## Reuse sources

The rmcp 3.9.0 transport and the action registry (S04); the `app_user(kind='agent')` bearer (S06b); the `run`, `approval` and `approval_decision` tables with the `runs.*` and `approvals.list|decide` actions (S06); and the `runs.cancel` state machine. Migration 0023 adds two indexes and nothing else.

## Inception units

Four: the Phase A set (stakeholders, drivers, requirements, concept), the Phase B capability map, the Phase C data entities and the Phase D standards. Each is one authored artefact in this pack.

## Dependencies

S04 supplies the registry and transport, S05 the project and card actions, S06 the run and approval state machines, and S06b the licence principal. S13 populates the task status message; the agent's own task support is a separate plan.

## Acceptance

`acceptance/programme/S06c.toml` at the pinned snapshot. The gate is the task round trip through a project that waits on an approval, and the compiled-registry assertion is the one that cannot be faked by a serialised flag.

## Capabilities

Two: durable execution (start a project and stop listening) and deferred answer (resolve a blocked project through the same protocol). Both reuse the run and approval state machines; neither adds a surface.

## Plan

The work is complete and the record is being supplied retrospectively. The operative order was migration, contract, surface, parity; the remaining work is none in this project, and the push and percentage requests are new units rather than defects here.

closure_review:
# Closure Review — S06c MCP Tasks (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The outcome is a durable agent task with no second store. Against the manifest's checks, every one the manifest can run is green at the snapshot: the compiled-registry assertion, the project-scoped listing, the answer path, the terminal ordering and the single ownership error code. The retrospective level is compliant for the record set because the pack supplies the lifecycle and the receipt proves it.

## Evidence

`acceptance/programme/S06c.toml` with its seventeen checks, the receipt `docs/evidence/rework/S06c.json` at the pinned snapshot, the contract and parity suites, and migration `0023_s06c_mcp_tasks.sql` with its two indexes. The corrected compiled-registry assertion is named in the review findings so the earlier zero-match form is not reintroduced.

## Open items

None in this project's scope. The push channel and progress percentage are separate units by the slice plan's boundary; the agent's own task support is a separate plan; and `statusMessage` is S13's to populate.

## Decision

Close the record set as compliant and keep the project closed. The decision is a record decision: it asserts that the lifecycle exists and is proved on the paths the manifest runs, and it asserts nothing about push delivery, progress reporting or a deployed agent application.
